evidence.note: Claim: a failed multi-reviewer round records the status-ranked identifying reviewer (min status + cross-family tie-break) as the failing reviewer. Mechanism: _record_review names best.reviewer, chosen by _identifying_reviewer. Refutation: a clean cross-family reviewer would be named on a failed gate. Test: tests/test_review_failed_names_failing_reviewer.py — on unfixed code it asserted ev['reviewer']=='failing' but got 'clean' (FAIL); after the fix it passed.

Memory/lessons consulted: ddflow_configured_reviewers (critic includes gemini), pytest-bash-denied rule (tests run via ddflow gates), r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY). AGENTS.md four rules applied: reviewer that cannot run = unavailable; cross-family reviewer required. No rule contradicted.

Regression test first (failed pre-fix, passed post-fix). Fix: extracted _blocking_findings in records.py and _failing_reviewer in run.py; _review_gate now names the reviewer whose blocking finding failed the gate. Files: ddflow/api/review/records.py, ddflow/api/review/run.py, tests/test_review_failed_names_failing_reviewer.py. ruff check+format clean; _review_gate CC stays at 20 (grade C).

chunk_findings.detail: When `_gate_outcome` returns `"failed"` from the full re-review branch after `blocking` is empty (records.py after `if blocking:` -> “A full re-review must not converge … while a confirmed … still standing”), `_failing_reviewer` recomputes `_blocking_findings`, gets `[]`, and falls back to `best`. If `best` is a clean reviewer with 0 findings, the record still says `failed (reviewer <clean>)`, the exact bug this change claims to fix. Concrete input: prior `chunk_findings` contain one still-standing confirmed defect; a converging full re-review has `results = [clean_reviewer_0_findings (selected as best), low_finding_reviewer]`; the low finding is below `cfg.review.converge_floor` and is not the prior defect. `RV.blocking_findings` returns `[]`, `_gate_outcome` returns `"failed"` because the prior finding is still standing, and `_failing_reviewer` names the clean reviewer.

chunk_findings.detail: `_failing_reviewer` relies on object identity (`any(b is f for b in blocking for f in r.findings)`) to map blocking findings back to the reviewer that produced them. If `RV.blocking_findings` (or any underlying data transformation) returns newly instantiated finding objects or copies rather than the exact same object references held in `r.findings`, `is` identity comparison will fail, `_failing_reviewer` will find no match, and it will fall back to returning `best` (defeating the fix and leaving the bug present when findings are rebuilt or filtered by value).

data.probe: _blocking_findings never reinstantiates findings: it flattens the exact Finding objects each ReviewResult.findings held, and RV.blocking_findings returns list(findings) (non-converged) or [f for f in findings if ...] (converged) -- the same objects, never copies. The is-identity match is precise (and more precise than digest matching, which mis-attributes two reviewers' byte-identical findings). The end-to-end test test_a_failed_review_names_the_reviewer_that_found_the_blocking_defect exercises this path and passes.

chunk_findings.detail: The change switches the triage-scope call from `best` to `named`. The new docstring says `best` is the identifying pass and that naming the failing reviewer must not re-purpose a PARTIAL reviewer as the identifying pass, but `_say_triage_scope` is the function that reports the identifying pass's triage scope/coverage, and its third argument was `best` before this change. When `named` is a distinct failing reviewer (possibly PARTIAL), this call now reports the failing reviewer's scope instead of the identifying pass's, contradicting the comment and producing output inconsistent with the record evidence that deliberately keeps `best`'s status/coverage. Concrete input: `outcome == "failed"` with `best` a full pass and `named` a partial reviewer whose finding blocked the gate; the console triage scope is then printed from the partial reviewer rather than the full identifying pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/gate.py:306 (`_say_triage_scope(say, results, named)`)

chunk_findings.detail: The diff removes the only assignment of `prior` from `_gate_outcome` and now obtains `blocking, converged_round` from `_blocking_findings`, but `_blocking_findings` returns only `(blocking, converged_round)`; it does not return `prior`. The unchanged full re-review branch immediately after the visible hunk still implements the comment “A full re-review must not converge … while a confirmed … still standing” by checking `_still_standing(it, gate, prior.get("chunk_findings"))`. In that branch `prior` is now undefined. Concrete input: a converged full re-review whose current findings are below the converge floor while a confirmed finding from the previous round is still standing reaches that line with `blocking == []`; instead of returning `"failed"`, it raises `NameError: name 'prior' is not defined`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/records.py:_gate_outcome

chunk_findings.detail: When `_blocking_findings` returns an empty `blocking`, the new fallback `return identifying` still reproduces the original bug on the confirmed-unrechecked path. Concrete input: `_gate_outcome` returns `"failed"` from the full re-review branch because a prior-round confirmed finding is still standing; `_blocking_findings` is empty since no current reviewer found a fresh block, so `_failing_reviewer` returns `identifying`, a clean current reviewer with 0 findings. The returned review data then has `"outcome": "failed"` and `"reviewer": identifying.reviewer`, so the current run still reports `failed (reviewer <clean>)`. The triage says the failure is already recorded against the prior reviewer, but that does not answer the user-visible current-run output this code still emits.

chunk_findings.detail: Line 306 now passes `named` to `_say_triage_scope(say, results, named)`, while the comment added to `_record_review` explicitly says the partial failing reviewer must not replace `best` as the identifying pass because it would misstate the round’s coverage. The original call passed `best`, and `_say_triage_scope` is the scope-reporting helper; for a full `best` with 10 findings and a partial failing `named` with 2 findings, the recorded evidence keeps `best`’s coverage but the user-facing triage-scope line reports `named`’s 2, which is exactly the coverage misstatement the change says it must avoid.

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback `return identifying` still reproduces the B3113b1f522 bug for the full re-review branch where `_gate_outcome` returns `"failed"` but `_blocking_findings` is empty because the failure is a still-standing confirmed prior finding. In that branch the function returns the clean `identifying` reviewer, and `_review_gate` then emits `"reviewer": named.reviewer` with zero findings for an `outcome` of `"failed"`. The `named`/`identifying` split does not answer this case; it only fixes non-empty `_blocking_findings`. The prior probe says no current reviewer found a fresh defect, but the code still writes a current clean reviewer's name onto the failed review.

chunk_findings.detail: `_failing_reviewer` relies on object identity (`any(b is f for b in blocking for f in r.findings)`) to map blocking findings back to the reviewer that produced them.
